name: Driving test prep
intro: Where the questions match the real DMV exam, and where it is a stale question bank and paywall traps.

apps.title: DMV Genie: Permit Test 2026
apps.verdict: One of the more accurate trainers: questions are close to the real exam, there are explanations and a missed-question bank, and many pass CDL and regular tests on the first try. Downsides are that half the material sits behind a subscription, questions repeat, and a few answers are wrong.
apps.loved: Questions close to the real test, answer explanations, missed-question review bank, strong CDL prep, clean interface
apps.weak: Half the material behind a paywall, repeating questions, occasional wrong answers, purchase restore trouble on a new device, charged after cancelling the trial
apps.whoFor: People prepping for a regular test or CDL who want a reliable trainer alongside the official state manual.

quotes.text: I bought a $39 app to get my license. I spent two weeks taking the practice tests. The questions started repeating after a short while. However, during the actual DMV exam, I didn't encounter a single question from the app.

apps.title: CDL Prep Test 2026
apps.verdict: A free trainer covering the whole CDL spectrum including endorsements, and many pass GK and doubles/triples on it first try. But overlap with the real exam swings by state and is thin on HAZMAT, with some answers not matching the DMV booklet. Explanations are scarce and question grammar is often clumsy.
apps.loved: Free and covers the full CDL set at once: general knowledge, air brakes, doubles/triples, tanker, hazmat. Good for warming up and reviewing before the exam, many pass GK first try.
apps.weak: Overlap with the real state test is weak and inconsistent, especially on HAZMAT. There are wrong answers, lots of grammar slips, and questions that read like machine translation. Ads pop every 5-10 questions and are easy to mis-tap.
apps.whoFor: People stacking several CDL endorsements who want a free run through the base before the exam. For safety pair it with the official booklet and double-check disputed answers.

quotes.text: AI generated with lots of mistakes... Gives me multiple Texas specific questions when I had Mississippi selected. No idea why this app is so highly rated.
Live in South Carolina, downloaded this for HAZMAT, learned all 119 questions just for only 8 out of the 30 at the DMV to be on this app.
Used this app to study and pass the GK, doubles- triples, and tanker. Currently studying for hazmat. Really good to practice and pre test .

apps.title: Pennsylvania DMV - Permit test
apps.verdict: This is a free Pennsylvania-specific app, and it basically works. People prepare and pass the exam on the first try. The main downside is ads right in the middle of a test that break focus and sometimes kill an attempt.
apps.loved: It helps build confidence before the exam and genuinely prepares you for the permit. Nice design, different modes, access to the handbook. Many passed and are grateful.
apps.weak: Ads every couple of questions are the top complaint in nearly every review. One long ad even counted a test as failed. There are wrong answers, typos, and odd wording, and the stats counter sometimes shows unfinished on a completed test.
apps.whoFor: For Pennsylvania residents willing to tolerate ads for free prep. Those who cannot stand ads mid-task should look at a paid option.

apps.title: CDL Test Prep 2026
apps.verdict: A solid CDL trainer: the air brakes and combinations sections helped many pass on the first try, and the missed-question review works well. But there are factual slips in answers (it confuses 8 and 10 hours in the sleeper berth), some questions are off-topic for the class you need, ads are heavy, and sometimes wrong-state questions pop up.
apps.loved: Strong air brakes and combinations sections, missed-question review, free access to the bank, helps you get your CLP
apps.weak: Factual errors in answers, questions off-topic for your class, heavy ads, occasional wrong-state questions, the app heats the phone and drains the battery
apps.whoFor: Aspiring truck drivers prepping for the CDL who will double-check questionable answers against the manual.

apps.title: CDL Prep
apps.verdict: A solid general-knowledge trainer, people really pass CDL on it. But the answer key has recurring errors: questions about stopping distance of empty versus loaded trucks are keyed wrong, and the app marks the correct answer as incorrect. Hazmat coverage is weak, and ads every two questions in practice mode seriously get in the way of studying.
apps.loved: Prepares you well for general knowledge, many pass the next day after cramming. The exam mode and question repetition land well, and the GK content is called among the best.
apps.weak: The answer key has recurring errors (stopping distance of empty versus loaded truck and bobtail), and the correct answer is marked wrong. Over half the hazmat exam questions are missing. Ads every 2 questions in practice mode, an accidental left swipe wipes all progress, and the screen freezes.
apps.whoFor: People prepping for CDL general knowledge who can tolerate ads or stay in exam mode. For hazmat and disputed braking questions, cross-check with another source.

quotes.text: This app needs to have it's answer key reviewed. Several questions in the pool will mark your answer incorrect then proceed to explain the reasons the answer is correct. i.e. You answer a loaded truck takes longer to stop than an empty. It marks empty truck as the correct answer.

Most of the questions for general knowledge from the app appeared on the test, but with hazmat more than half of the questions that were on the test weren't in the app. Still a great app for general knowledge but I recommend looking somewhere else for hazmat.

apps.title: Zutobi: Permit & Driving Prep
apps.verdict: The short game-style lessons work well for beginners, but the app asks you to pay almost immediately after you pick your state, and the free tier gives you almost nothing. Some users found questions on the real exam that were never in the app, and deeper topics like new-driver restrictions are covered thinly.
apps.loved: Short clear lessons, game-like format, explanations before you answer, gets you into the material fast
apps.weak: Paywall right after install with no way out, charged on day one of the trial, skips key exam topics, some questions did not match the real test
apps.whoFor: Beginners who are fine paying for a subscription and prefer learning in small bites rather than from a manual.

apps.title: DMV Practice Test 2026: Permit
apps.verdict: For some the questions match the exam word for word, for others almost nothing matched after memorizing 400+ terms. Recent versions broke the images in questions, so you cannot see them and have to guess. Ads pop every 2-3 questions, and answer explanations and detailed results are hidden behind a subscription.
apps.loved: Many find the questions close to the real exam, and the practice tests build confidence right before the DMV. A pleasant first-use experience and handy pre-test drilling.
apps.weak: Test overlap is inconsistent, with states (WA) and cases where almost nothing matched after memorizing hundreds of terms. Recent versions fail to load images in questions, forcing guesses. Very heavy ads every 2-3 questions, and mistake explanations and detailed results are subscription-only.
apps.whoFor: People who want a quick confidence trainer the day before the permit test and can tolerate ads or pay for pro. Check that question images actually load for you.

quotes.text: i am really liking the setup and questions of the app but i would like to be able to take a break from the long streak of questions but it doesn't save my progress in the individual tests
This app is useful but almost all of images provided on the app aren't available to see. At this point i just have to guess what the photo is when answering questions.

apps.title: Georgia DDS - GA Permit test
apps.verdict: This free Georgia-specific app genuinely helps prepare for the permit, with happy parents and teens. The main trouble is ads after almost every question that break concentration. Some warn that the question bank does not cover the full scope and you can fail without the official book.
apps.loved: It helps learn signs and rules and prepares you for the written exam. Parents find it handy to study with their kids, and the reward system motivates. Flashcards and the handbook are on hand.
apps.weak: Ads after every three or four questions are the top complaint in nearly all reviews, and even a blocker does not help. Some questions do not match the real test and the bank does not cover the full scope, which is why people failed at DDS.
apps.whoFor: For Georgia residents willing to tolerate ads and back up their study with the official handbook. Not as the sole source, the bank is incomplete.

apps.title: Drivers Ed: DMV Permit Test
apps.verdict: The app genuinely helped a lot of people prepare and pass, with plenty of tests and questions. But a recurring bug keeps flipping the correct answer when a question repeats, and the review screen highlights two answers at once. There are also complaints that few of the app's questions showed up on the real exam.
apps.loved: Lots of free mock tests you can run as many times as you want. People like how easy and even fun the studying is, and several reviews mention passing the exam.
apps.weak: Answers sometimes get muddled: you pick the right one and it counts as wrong, then on the repeat the correct answer is a different option. The review screen highlights two answers at once. Some people found none of the app's questions on the real test, and a purchased ad-removal was lost after switching phones.
apps.whoFor: People who want to run free mock tests over and over and do not mind double-checking disputed answers against the manual.

quotes.text: I have been going over the answers at the end of each test and the app changes the answers. If you finish a test go through every question and take a few more tests and the answers will change for a few questions.

apps.title: New York DMV NY - Permit test
apps.verdict: A state-specific trainer for NY, and overlap with the real permit test is high: people say the NYC test is almost a copy of the app and pass after a day of cramming. Flashcards and the marathon test prepare you well. The main and nearly only issue is a barrage of ads every 1-2 minutes, some inappropriate for teens.
apps.loved: Accurate match to the real NY permit test, people call it a copy of the app and pass after a day of prep. Flashcards and the marathon mode are handy, you can study on the commute and ease pre-test stress.
apps.weak: Ads literally every 1-2 minutes, after every question, and some cannot be closed and open the App Store, freezing the app. Some ads are inappropriate for the teens who are the ones prepping for the permit. In places you have to wait 30 seconds after a question.
apps.whoFor: Teens and adults in New York State who want an accurate trainer for the local permit test. Be ready to endure a lot of ads or find a way to remove them.

quotes.text: So just took my permit and passed. I studied for like a day until I got at least 1 out of 20 wrong or all correct and when I tell you the nyc real permit test is copy and paste I'm not joking it's literally the same damn thing this app is worth studying for !!

apps.title: CDL Prep Practice Test Genie
apps.verdict: A full ELDT course with videos and handbook-based questions, and people really pass hazmat and endorsements with top scores on it. But it is a repackaged DMV Genie at a higher price, and the payment side works badly: purchased subscriptions vanish, extra charges appear, and promised lifetime access gets lost.
apps.loved: A well-organized ELDT course: videos, handbook-aligned questions, coverage of all endorsements. People pass hazmat and other tests first try, often a month of prep is enough.
apps.weak: Billing breaks down: lifetime subscriptions disappear, double and surprise charges happen, and the listed price differs from the checkout price. Content costs more than DMV Genie from the same developer with the same substance. Sometimes the ELDT certificate does not show after completion.
apps.whoFor: People who specifically need a structured ELDT course for hazmat or endorsements and are willing to pay for a month subscription. Before buying, compare the price with DMV Genie and watch your charges.

apps.title: DMV Driver License Permit Test
apps.verdict: The app genuinely helps and is praised mostly by Spanish-speaking users who passed the exam. But the Spanish translation is nonsensical in places, as if from Google Translate, and for some the practice test crashes on launch. Lots of ads.
apps.loved: It shows the correct answers after each question, handy for people who are not tech-savvy. Spanish-speaking users are grateful and describe getting their license after studying in the app.
apps.weak: The Spanish translation is poor and sometimes meaningless, diverging from the handbook. For some people the practice test crashes right on opening even after reinstalling. Ads get in the way of studying.
apps.whoFor: For those studying in English and willing to put up with ads. Spanish speakers should double-check the wording, the translation lets them down.

apps.title: CDL Prep Practice Test - 2026
apps.verdict: It genuinely helps many pass the CDL, the air-brake question images get praise, and the flashcards work. But some of the glowing reviews read suspiciously smooth, and sober ones note exam questions that weren't in the app and charges for a subscription never signed up for.
apps.loved: The question style matches the exam in several states, air-brake images and flashcards help, and people pass all sections first try.
apps.weak: The AI repeats a question three or four times per quiz, there's no theory before the test, some questions didn't match the DMV, and it charges for a subscription you never set up.
apps.whoFor: CDL candidates, especially for air brakes where the images help. Check your subscriptions and don't trust the glowing reviews alone.

quotes.text: Half the questions in here are not on the exam for Class B... The passenger endorsement I also failed using this app.

It doesnt give me the option to retake the same questions if i have some of the wrong after im done with the 10 or 20 questions it gives me different questions instead of letting me correct the ones i have wrong
What helped was seeing pics with the questions. Way easier to get what they're talking about when you can actually see the parts instead of just reading about em.

apps.title: Aceable Drivers Ed & Test Prep
apps.verdict: This is a full drivers ed course, not just a question trainer, with videos and text that many find easier than classroom lessons. But it costs more than rivals, support is weak, and the completion certificate sometimes arrives late or fails to load, which gets people turned away at the DMV. There are complaints about clashes with specific state requirements and pushed add-on services.
apps.loved: Full course with video and text, explains things more clearly than class, mini-checks keep you focused, teens like it
apps.weak: Pricier than rivals, certificate arrives late or fails to load, weak support, pushed add-ons at signup, some data conflicts with state requirements
apps.whoFor: Teens and parents who need a full online drivers ed course with a certificate, not just test questions.

apps.title: DMV WRITTEN TEST
apps.verdict: The content is free and actually decent: questions resemble the real test and wrong answers come with explanations. But ads wreck the experience, 30-60 second clips drop in mid-practice and break your flow. It also lacks pictures for the road signs.
apps.loved: Free access, questions resemble the real test, explanations for wrong answers, retake option
apps.weak: Too many ads right during the test, long clips break your flow, pop-up ads lose your current question, few sign images
apps.whoFor: People who need free access and can tolerate heavy ads for the sake of practice.

quotes.text: It shows me the right answer when I get it wrong and I can always go back and re do the test if I don't get it the first time!

apps.title: DMV Driving Test Driver Start
apps.verdict: The flashcard-and-sections format is handy and some pass permit first try. But many say almost none of the exam questions appeared in the app and that the signs look AI-generated. There are errors: in the intersection questions the correct answer contradicts the explanation, and some items are factually wrong.
apps.loved: Handy format: flashcards, category breakdown, and you can read the material manually too. Helps many feel more confident, some pass permit first try.
apps.weak: Overlap with the real test is often weak, up to 19 of 20 unfamiliar questions. Signs and some questions look AI-generated and are not on the actual permit. There are key and logic errors (intersection, age and alcohol), and ads disrupt the test run.
apps.whoFor: People who want a visual flashcard trainer to review the basics. Better used alongside the official handbook rather than instead of it.

quotes.text: Can you fix the explanation on the question... The correct answer does not match the explanation given.

apps.title: CDL Prep Practice Test: 2026
apps.verdict: For CDL prep the app is popular and many pass quickly, with the endorsement coverage and practice tests praised. But an alarming complaint recurs: a noticeable share of questions have wrong information or wording not from the CDL book. Plus confusion over the annual subscription charge.
apps.loved: More convenient than the outdated paper handbook, it prepares you for different endorsements like school bus and passengers. People pass in a couple of weeks and praise the clear, realistic tests.
apps.weak: By users' estimates about 5-7 percent of questions carry wrong information, and some wording does not match the state CDL book. There are questions missing needed data, blank screens, and doubled answers. The annual subscription gets charged again monthly.
apps.whoFor: For future CDL drivers as a trainer alongside the official book, with mandatory double-checking of questionable answers. Not as the sole source before the exam.

quotes.text: Half the questions in here are not on the exam for Class B... The passenger endorsement I also failed using this app.

It doesnt give me the option to retake the same questions if i have some of the wrong after im done with the 10 or 20 questions it gives me different questions instead of letting me correct the ones i have wrong
What helped was seeing pics with the questions. Way easier to get what they're talking about when you can actually see the parts instead of just reading about em.

apps.title: Alabama  DMV - AL Permit test
apps.verdict: A free prep app for the Alabama permit test: some got 90% overlap and an easy pass, others failed because the wording differed. The shared pain point is ads popping up every few questions and badly breaking focus.
apps.loved: Completely free with plenty of tests. Some people studied for a month and passed on the first try, and a few reviews claim 90% overlap with the real exam.
apps.weak: Ads every few questions, sometimes inappropriate for teens. The real test is worded differently, and some people failed after studying only with the app. There are also typos, freezes, and buggy score counting.
apps.whoFor: People prepping for the Alabama permit test who can tolerate ads for a free tool and also read the official manual so the different wording does not catch them out.

apps.title: DMV Permit Prep 2026 - Exam
apps.verdict: A free trainer with a nice layout and post-answer explanations, and many pass the test with it. But there's a notable bug where the road-sign images just don't load, making sign questions impossible to pass. The premium ad sometimes covers the continue button, and some questions differ from the real test, especially after moving to another state.
apps.loved: Free access, handy layout, explanations after each answer, helps you pass the permit
apps.weak: Road-sign images don't load, the premium ad covers the continue button, sometimes two correct answers, some questions did not match the real test, occasional freezes
apps.whoFor: People who want a free trainer with explanations and can live with the sign-image bug.

quotes.text: No payment needed, easy to use, explains the answer after you submit
It was great for my new york permit but i moved to north carolina and had to get a new one… i failed because i studied from this app cuz its so different from the actual test
i'm noticing that the "What does this sign mean?" questions are glitched out to where you can't see the sign and there's nothing i can do but get the question wrong

apps.title: DMV Driving Permit Test Prep
apps.verdict: Some pass on it in a couple of days without reading the handbook, but many pay for the full bank and still fail because the real test asks different questions. Even the paid version has incomplete overlap, and images of signs fail to load in many questions. Some answers are outdated and the purchase does not carry between devices.
apps.loved: Helps you drill quickly and ease test anxiety, especially for people who failed permit before. The flashcards and section breakdown land well, some pass after a day or two of prep.
apps.weak: Even the paid full question set does not cover the real test, people fail after weeks of prep. Sign images fail to display in many questions because the image source is dead. There are outdated answers and typos, and the purchase is not always available on another device.
apps.whoFor: People who want light on-the-go practice and to calm nerves before the permit test. For a guarantee you will still need to work through your local DMV site and its quizzes.

apps.title: DMV Practice Test - 2026
apps.verdict: A simple, clear app where many found the questions nearly matched the real exam and passed on the first try. But just as many failed because the bank is outdated and does not line up with their state's test. The outcome depends heavily on your state and luck.
apps.loved: A simple, clear interface with questions often close to the real test. People studied for a couple of days and passed on the first try, praising the lack of filler questions.
apps.weak: The bank is outdated and in several states diverges from the real test, with wrong answers like wheel position on a downhill slope. Progress sometimes resets on its own. The question count does not always match the real state exam.
apps.whoFor: For those who want a quick feel for the format and will double-check the material on their state's DMV site. Do not rely on it alone, the bank is outdated in places.

apps.title: DMV Practice Test 2026 OneDMV
apps.verdict: An app with a gamified design and pleasant rewards for a completed test, with questions close to the real ones. But essentially only one lesson is free, then a paywall, and the subscription is demanded by card right at entry and is hard to cancel. Many typos and grammar errors in the questions.
apps.loved: Real questions and answers, a pleasant reward system with a cheerful sound after success. It helps break down the details of the rules and prepares you for the exam.
apps.weak: Almost everything is behind a paywall after the first lesson, canceling the subscription is hard, and the cancel settings are nowhere to be found. Typos and weak grammar in questions throw you off, and wrong answers turn up. The free version gives only three lives.
apps.whoFor: For those willing to take a paid subscription who want a gamified prep format. For a quick free look, only the first lesson will do.

quotes.text: Funciona bien y se ve profesional, pero no explica las respuestas incorrectas, solo las correctas. Hay que volver a hacer todo el examen (10-15 preguntas) intentar responder bien y obtener la explicación.

apps.title: CA DMV Permit Test Now
apps.verdict: For the California test the questions are often near-identical and people pass first try. But results are inconsistent: some scored 95% steadily and still failed, questions repeat, images stopped loading, and ads hit after every action.
apps.loved: Questions are often close to the real CA test, you can save missed ones into a separate run, and many pass first try after practicing.
apps.weak: Questions repeat and some aren't from the exam, images fail to load and show a question mark, the app freezes and crashes, ads after every test, plus complaints of data harvesting and scam texts.
apps.whoFor: Californians as their main practice, but not the only source. Add fresh topics like NEV and hand signals from the manual.

quotes.text: I was getting 100% on the tests on the app. I went to take the test and bombed it. Terrible app do not use!!!!!!

apps.title: DMV: Practice Test 2026 Permit
apps.verdict: A free trainer with a clear set of tests, and some people pass on the first try. But many failed the exam because the app's questions differed noticeably from the real ones, with New Jersey and California drawing the most complaints. Ads push into the test, progress isn't saved, and one user's one-time premium purchase vanished and asked to be paid for again.
apps.loved: Free access, clear set of tests, review of your own mistakes, helped some pass on the first try
apps.weak: Questions often don't match the real test, ads block your progress, progress isn't saved, one-time premium purchase disappears, sometimes you can't select an answer
apps.whoFor: People who want to run free tests but will read the official state manual alongside it.

quotes.text: i am really liking the setup and questions of the app but i would like to be able to take a break from the long streak of questions but it doesn't save my progress in the individual tests
This app is useful but almost all of images provided on the app aren't available to see. At this point i just have to guess what the photo is when answering questions.

apps.title: DMV Practice Test 2026 | Max
apps.verdict: The Duolingo-style format and detailed explanations are liked, but almost all content is paywalled and the bank itself is weak. There is outdated data like the wrong following distance in Kentucky, typos, and questions with multiple correct answers. Overlap with the real DMV, especially on endorsements, is low, and there are complaints about charges after canceling.
apps.loved: A pleasant Duolingo-like interface and detailed, clear explanations. Repetitive questions help drill the basics, and some get their permit on the app alone.
apps.weak: Almost everything is paywalled with a short trial. The bank has outdated facts (Kentucky following distance), typos, and questions where several answers are correct but only one counts. Overlap with the DMV on hazmat and passenger is low. There are charges after cancellation and no Spanish at all.
apps.whoFor: People who like a gamified format and will pay a subscription for handy explanations. Do not rely on it alone for endorsements and state-specific rules.

quotes.text: The app says the following distance rule in Kentucky is three seconds, but the official DMV manual actually specifies four seconds as the safe following distance.

apps.title: Alabama DMV Permit Practice
apps.verdict: This Alabama-specific app does help you prepare, and there are people who passed the permit. But the ads are so heavy they interrupt studying every couple of questions, and after a redesign much of it went behind a subscription. People are annoyed by the changed rules and the flood of ads.
apps.loved: It covers basic signs and driving situations well and genuinely helps pass the permit. The smart learning for a small fee is seen as worth it, and some passed on the first try.
apps.weak: Too many ads, a 45-second clip literally every two or three questions. After the update only the mock test is free, the rest behind a subscription, though it used to be free. Premium sometimes unlocks only some cards, and progress gets reset.
apps.whoFor: For Alabama residents willing to tolerate ads or pay for smart learning. Those who counted on the old free version will be disappointed.

apps.title: Massachusetts RMV  Permit test
apps.verdict: The road-sign material is decent, but the exam covers more than the app does. The bigger problem is the ads that pop up every three to five questions and shred the whole session.
apps.loved: As a supplement to the manual it helps drill signs, and some do pass after using it.
apps.weak: Ads after every few questions drive people crazy, the questions don't match the real RMV test, there's no review of missed answers, and the score counter sometimes reads low.
apps.whoFor: People already reading the official Massachusetts manual who want to drill signs. The app alone won't get you through the exam.

quotes.text: You will not get similar questions from this app. I got only 2-3% of similar questions. It's better if read the manual and prepare for the exam.
In my opinion , should have explanations in each question after you answer it.

apps.title: DMV Practice Test 2026 myDMV
apps.verdict: A pleasant interface hides a heavy paywall: it won't show your test results without payment, and you can barely do anything for free. The bank has errors, outdated state manuals, and signs of generative-AI text, plus some state mix-ups. Some people pass the exam with it, but relying on it alone is risky.
apps.loved: Easy navigation, some questions match the real test, most-missed-question trainer
apps.weak: Test results locked until you pay, outdated state manuals, wrong answers, theory reads like generative-AI text, state mix-ups, heavy subscription ads
apps.whoFor: People willing to pay and to double-check questionable answers against the official state manual.

quotes.text: Weirdly, my profile has me studying for the CT test, but the actual studying is giving me the California specifics for some reason. Must just be a bug.
this app has actual questions from the REAL test!! ... even has an option to quiz your most missed questions. definitely recommend.

apps.title: DMV Practice Test Permit 2025
apps.verdict: The 4.8 rating rests on a five-stars-to-kill-ads scheme, so the score can't be trusted. The real pain is the subscription: $25 a month charged instantly under a 'free trial,' with canceling and refunds a struggle.
apps.loved: For those who pay it helps close knowledge gaps, the flashcards are useful, and beginners like it as an intro to the rules.
apps.whoFor: Beginners willing to pay a monthly subscription and check the trial terms in advance. Don't trust the store rating, read the review text.

apps.title: DMV Permit Test 2025 Cdl Study
apps.verdict: Those who pay the one-time price often praise it and pass both permit and CDL from this one app. But the free branding misleads, everything quickly hits a paywall, and a plagiarism accusation from a competitor hangs over the content.
apps.loved: The one-time purchase pays off, questions are accurate and varied, missed answers are explained, and many pass permit and CDL first try on it alone.
apps.weak: Billed as free while almost everything costs money, a near-hundred-dollar price appears, some questions lack images, the app sometimes won't launch, and a content-copying accusation lingers.
apps.whoFor: Permit or CDL candidates willing to pay a one-time price and not expecting free. For sign-image questions back yourself up with the manual.

quotes.text: I purchased this to prep for CDL to drive a school bus... I answered over 1,600 questions total. I did not read any of the manual. I only used this app. I went to the DMV and aced all 5

apps.title: Pass Permit Test DMV -Drivify
apps.verdict: The app promises easy prep, and those who reach the content do pass. But too many people pay for a subscription and get no access, left with one test of eleven questions. The billing problem has repeated for years and hurts trust.
apps.loved: Clear presentation of the rules, nice graphics, and the chance to fix your mistakes. People share that they studied on their own and with family and passed the written exam.
apps.weak: The main trouble is billing: the subscription is charged but tests beyond the first do not unlock. Sign images fail to load, so you answer sign questions blind. The help button leads to an unrelated Facebook page.
apps.whoFor: For those who find the free first test enough to get a feel for the format. Paying for a subscription is risky until the unlock is fixed.

quotes.text: The questions about the signage, are supposed to have images, but none load when the question is asked.

apps.title: California DMV Test
apps.verdict: The study part is decent and helps many pass, but billing is broken. Accounts lose data within a week, purchases vanish and the app demands money again, and some content stays locked behind a repeat upgrade.
apps.loved: The material primes your brain for test mode, the interface is simple, and plenty pass the written exam after it.
apps.weak: Progress and payment disappear, the course asks to be bought again, there are typos and stale figures like the damage threshold, and some questions sit behind an upgrade.
apps.whoFor: Californians willing to risk losing access they paid for. Keep your receipt in case you need a refund dispute.

apps.title: DMV Permit Practice Test: Luma
apps.verdict: The storefront 4.83 does not match the text, where the real average is around 4.08. Two main issues: a hard paywall after 5-6 questions and factual errors in answers. In the right-of-way topic every option was marked wrong, the school bus question is keyed wrong, and on the Nevada permit only half the questions matched.
apps.loved: It helps some as a reference and review, the tap-to-open explanations are clear, and the test gives new questions each time. As a light warm-up for a beginner it sometimes works.
apps.weak: The paywall kicks in after 5-6 questions, almost everything is paid, and the roughly $6-a-week subscription feels like a trap. There are factually wrong answers: in the right-of-way topic every option was marked wrong and the school bus question is keyed wrong. On the real Nevada permit only half the questions matched and one person failed.
apps.whoFor: Hardly anyone paying. The free limit of 5-6 questions is too small and the answer key cannot be trusted, better to grab the official state handbook.

apps.title: DMV 2026 Permit Practice Test
apps.verdict: The storefront shows almost five stars, but real reviews split in two. Some passed and praise how close it is to the real test, others failed on wrong answers and complain about money taken from their accounts. The gap between the store score and what real people write is too wide.
apps.loved: Those who passed note the clean interface and questions that follow real exam logic. People say they studied on the app and passed the California test on the first try.
apps.weak: Some questions do not match the real test, and there are wrong facts like the residential speed limit. Sign images fail to load, progress tracking is broken, and money gets charged even without a purchase.
apps.whoFor: For those ready to take a risk and double-check answers against the official handbook. For reliable state-specific prep, better find an option without a questionable question bank.

apps.title: DriverEdToGo Driver Education
apps.verdict: A real driver's-ed course with videos and quizzes, kids finish it and pass. The trouble is the plumbing: login won't let you in after signup, the certificate costs extra and takes weeks, and support often goes silent.
apps.loved: The material actually teaches, the videos are liked, the course is finished fast, and some get the certificate mailed and pass at the DMV.
apps.weak: Login rejects even the right password, password resets never arrive, the certificate costs extra and goes missing, and support is hard to understand and quiet for weeks.
apps.whoFor: People who need the official course certificate and can tolerate billing and support hassle. Keep proof of your payments.

apps.title: CDL Prep Test 2026: Drivers ed
apps.verdict: The storefront stars do not match the text: the real review average is 2.8. The core problem is that all five exams in a section consist of the same questions, the same question repeats five or six times in a test, so there is barely any practice. On the real CDL in NC nothing matched, plus it is paid, with clumsy English and charges after the trial.
apps.loved: Someone managed to pass CDL B on it after very intense prep over a week and a half. That is where the upside ends.
apps.weak: The real review score is only 2.8. All five exams in a section repeat the same questions, one question comes up 5-6 times in a 50-question test, and different exams are identical. Overlap with the real CDL is low or none, with questions from other states. Paid, clumsy English, nagging rating prompts, and charges after the trial with no way to cancel.
apps.whoFor: Almost no one. If you are truly short on time, use a free alternative, the official CDL booklet and YouTube rather than paying for repeated questions.

quotes.text: I bought this app to study for my CDL permit, but all five exams in each section (General Knowledge, Air Brakes, and Passenger Endorsement) have the same questions. There's no variety, which makes the practice useless.

apps.title: Official CDL Test Prep: Iowa
apps.verdict: Gives false confidence. The question pool is too narrow and answer order never shuffles, so you memorize position instead of the rule. The real CDL exam has topics that never appear in the app.
apps.loved: A few passed studying only from it, and the reading sections are called genuinely useful.
apps.weak: The pool doesn't cover the exam, questions and answers get cut off and unreadable on iPhone, tests can't be retaken, and the subscription keeps charging after you cancel.
apps.whoFor: At best a first look at CDL topics. Relying on it alone is risky, the real exam is far broader.

quotes.text: App keeps track of what you know and what you don't know so you can focus on the latter.

apps.title: DMV Practice Test・2026
apps.verdict: Only the download is free, past that you can't do anything without a subscription. Many users failed the real exam because two-thirds of the questions were different, there are outdated and plain wrong answers, and some answer choices don't display. There are complaints about charges after cancelling and sudden monthly billing.
apps.loved: Pleasant interface, several practice modes, some scenario questions are close to the real ones
apps.weak: Nothing available without a subscription, many questions did not match the real test, outdated and wrong answers, answer choices not displaying, hidden and ongoing charges
apps.whoFor: Honestly no one: too many content misses and billing questions, better to pick a more reliable trainer.

apps.title: CDL Permit: Practice Test 2026
apps.verdict: The design is pleasant, but the content lets it down: questions are clumsily worded, with typos and sometimes two correct answers, so you end up guessing the intended one. In practice the same question repeats many times, so you can't test the full scope of your knowledge. People fail the exam when relying on it, crashes and server issues are common, and there are complaints about paying $99 to no avail.
apps.loved: Pleasant design, helped some get their CDL, has a free bank
apps.weak: Clumsy wording and typos, one question repeats many times, wrong answers and two-correct answers, frequent crashes and server issues, questions diverge from the real CDL test
apps.whoFor: Honestly no one as a primary CDL trainer: too many errors and tech problems, a different app is safer.

quotes.text: It repeated the same question 15 out of the 30 questions on the practice test… half of the questions in the practice test were the same one. It's hard to test my knowledge on the full scope if I don't get to see most the questions..

apps.title: DMV Motorcycle Permit Test
apps.verdict: The app asks your state as if it'll tailor questions, but it serves metric speeds and signs that don't exist on American roads. Ads hit every three questions and often can't be closed because the X sits off the screen edge.
apps.loved: A few questions are lifted straight from the DMV sample test, and some with an accurate state pool manage to pass.
apps.weak: Speeds in kilometers and left-side driving betray non-US development, ads are unclosable, the app crashes on launch, and correct answers are sometimes marked wrong.
apps.whoFor: Honestly, almost no one in the US. Metric units and foreign signs outweigh the occasional good question.

apps.title: CDL Study · Practice Test 2026
apps.verdict: Dangerous because it teaches the wrong thing: correct answers get marked wrong, and it sometimes prompts the wrong action outright. Wording is in broken English, questions jump between languages, and errors and typos abound.
apps.loved: Spanish speakers like that content exists in Spanish and covers the CDL basics, and some call it convenient.
apps.weak: Correct answers flagged as wrong and teaching mistakes, broken English, language switching mid-quiz, an unclosable game ad, and a hard-to-find cancel button.
apps.whoFor: Hard to recommend to anyone seriously. Studying from an app that confuses right and wrong means memorizing errors.

quotes.text: Contestas correctamente y la app dice que mi respuesta fue errónea! Veo que hacen 2 años había el mismo problema!!

apps.title: DMV Permit Practice Test 2026+
apps.verdict: The gap between the near five stars on the store and the real text average of 2.5 is huge. One test is free but repeats the same questions every time, and the rest costs money. Even after paying, people complain about duplicates, typos, and questions not for their state.
apps.loved: Short praise with no specifics. A couple of people hope the app will help them pass, but there are almost no detailed success stories.
apps.weak: One free test with frozen questions, the rest behind a paywall. Many duplicate questions even within a single test, typos, missing words, and questions not for the right state. People paid and got no access to materials before their exam.
apps.whoFor: Probably no one. Too many complaints about billing and question quality, with a real risk of failing the actual exam over wrong questions.

quotes.text: I just took 8 tests in the app and i notice that it's all the same questions. A lot of duplicates of the same question even within one test. One of the tests had 6 duplicates!

apps.title: DMV Practice Test : All States
apps.verdict: The app looks free but every tap hits a subscription wall, and the trial quietly charges you. Some people passed after grinding the tests, yet many say the questions never showed up on their real exam. A textbook paywall trap propped up by an a storefront star that diverges from review text.
apps.loved: Those who got past the wall and aced every practice test often passed on the first try, sometimes without even opening the official manual.
apps.weak: Almost everything is locked behind a subscription and the payment pop-up appears on every action. The free trial charges money and is hard to cancel. Some questions did not match the real exam, and there are repeats plus loading bugs on the answers.
apps.whoFor: Only for people ready to pay for the subscription upfront and just run through the question bank. Anyone looking for free prep is better off with the DMV manual from the state website.
